teams.heading: Fiji slump to three consecutive defeats after home loss to Scotland
teams.body: Fiji are currently bottom of the table following three consecutive defeats. In their last five matches, the national side has registered just one victory alongside four losses. This run of form includes a 17-33 home defeat against Scotland in their most recent fixture. In the current tournament, the Flying Fijians have lost all three of their games, scoring 49 points and conceding 145 to leave them with a point difference of minus 96.

teams.heading: Steve Borthwick secures England contract extension past the 2028 Six Nations
teams.body: The Rugby Football Union will extend head coach Steve Borthwick’s contract until the end of the 2028 Six Nations. Performance director Conor O’Shea confirmed the move, aiming to eliminate distractions before next year’s World Cup in Australia. Despite a "horrendous" Six Nations campaign where England won only one match, Borthwick retains the board's backing. However, O’Shea warned that his future remains conditional, stating, "Everyone knows it will be judged on the World Cup."

lead.why: The RFU's decision to extend Steve Borthwick's contract to avoid World Cup uncertainty is the day's dominant story across all major outlets.

teams.heading: Scotland winger applies performance psychology study to improve his on-field results
teams.body: A Scotland winger has revealed he is using himself as a "guinea pig" while pursuing a side hustle in performance psychology. This self-experimentation highlights a growing trend of psychological focus within the national squad. As the team prepares for the visit of New Zealand, such marginal gains could prove vital for a side currently sitting fifth in the standings.

teams.heading: Lock Ben Carter cleared for Dragons return after ankle injury with Wales
teams.body: Lock Ben Carter is fit to start the domestic season with Dragons after recovering from the ankle injury that forced him out of the July defeat to South Africa. The 25-year-old, who started six consecutive Tests before the training-ground blow, was on crutches during the summer but avoided surgery. Defence coach Dale MacLeod confirmed the lock is "keen, refreshed and ready" to return, providing a boost for the national side ahead of November's meeting with Japan.

lead.why: The return of a regular Test starter provides a key fitness boost following the heavy loss to South Africa.

teams.heading: Carter Gordon sidelined for two months following leg fracture in Argentina
teams.body: The Wallabies face a challenging period without first-choice flyhalf Carter Gordon, who is expected to miss two months of action after sustaining a leg fracture during Sunday’s draw with Argentina. The 25-year-old playmaker, who had established himself as a focal point under Les Kiss, is set to sit out the upcoming Test against South Africa and the Bledisloe Cup series. Ben Donaldson, who started in Mendoza, is currently the internal frontrunner to cover the position during Gordon’s recovery.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One confirms fixtures for upcoming 2026-27 season
teams.body: The Japan Rugby League One has released the full fixture list for the 2026-27 Division One campaign, which commences on 12 December. The 12-team competition will see each side play 18 matches, culminating in the playoff final on 6 June 2027. Defending champions Kobelco Kobe Steelers are set to host Toyota Verblitz in the opening round. The league confirmed that the matchups were determined by the final standings from two seasons ago to ensure competitive balance across the competition.

lead.why: The release of the full 2026-27 domestic fixture list is the most significant news for the Japanese rugby community today.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie prepares for final Test as injury list grows longer
teams.body: Coach Dave Rennie has confirmed plans to rotate his squad for the series decider, an initiative he insists was planned regardless of the previous result. The task is now complicated by the loss of Ardie Savea, Luke Jacobson and Quinn Tupaea to injury. With the series currently 2-1 in South Africa’s favour, Rennie remains bullish about his side’s chances, stating: “We have definitely got one more in us.” The squad is currently recovering following a gruelling 26-hour journey to the United States.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus rewards Morné van den Berg with pivotal starting spot
teams.body: Morné van den Berg has been promoted to the starting XV for the final Test against the All Blacks in Baltimore. Rassie Erasmus confirmed the move following the scrum-half’s impactful cameo in last weekend’s win, noting the player had to show significant resilience after injury struggles. While Cobus Reinach moves to the bench to provide experience, Erasmus insisted the change is based on merit, stating: "Morne made a fantastic impact when he took the field last week. He deserves a chance to start."
